authors: Zifan Ning; Can Li; He Chen; Guangyao Zhou; Shanghang Zhang; Lianlin Li; Yin Zhuang
title: Uncertainty-Aware Cross-Domain Few-Shot Scene Classification from Remote Sensing Imagery
venue: Remote Sensing
main_finding: Uses predictive uncertainty to improve robustness and knowledge transfer under remote-sensing domain discrepancy.
limitation: Few-shot target-domain setting differs from our source-only DG protocol.
relevance_to_our_work: Very recent evidence that domain discrepancy and uncertainty remain central RS classification problems.

authors: Sara A. Al-Emadi; Yin Yang; Ferda Ofli
title: Analysing Satellite Imagery Classification under Spatial Domain Shift across Geographic Regions
venue: International Journal of Computer Vision
method: DG benchmark; ERM; modern DG methods; foundation models
evaluation_protocol: Single- and multi-source geographic domain-shift testing
main_finding: Shows significant geographic distribution shift and reports that carefully configured ERM with strong representations can remain highly competitive with modern DG methods.
limitation: Satellite geographic shift differs from our composite UAV/satellite/source shift.
relevance_to_our_work: One of the closest recent studies to our central finding that DG interventions do not automatically beat ERM.

authors: Abhishek Kuriyal; Elliot Vincent; Mathieu Aubry; Loic Landrieu
title: CoDEx: Combining Domain Expertise for Spatial Generalization in Satellite Image Analysis
venue: CVPR Workshops (EarthVision)
main_finding: Shows domain-expert specialization and selection can improve spatial generalization across satellite datasets.
limitation: Different task/data regime and a more specialized multi-expert architecture.
relevance_to_our_work: Recent spatial-generalization comparison for satellite imagery.

authors: Yunxiao Qi; Dongyang Liu; Junping Zhang; Ye Zhang
title: A Shift Reduction Domain Generalization Network for Hyperspectral Image Cross-Domain Classification
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
main_finding: Proposes explicit feature/domain-shift reduction for hyperspectral cross-domain classification.
limitation: Hyperspectral spectral-spatial setting differs from RGB aerial scene classification.
relevance_to_our_work: Very recent remote-sensing DG evidence demonstrating continued interest in unseen-domain robustness.

authors: Kim VanExel; Samendra Sherchan; Siyan Liu
title: Optimizing Deep Learning Models for Climate-Related Natural Disaster Detection from UAV Images and Remote Sensing Data
venue: Journal of Imaging
main_finding: Demonstrates strong deep-learning performance for Flooded, Desert, and Neither classification on the Climate Change Dataset.
limitation: Does not provide the provenance-aware, source-disjoint, multi-seed, external-validation failure analysis used in our study.
relevance_to_our_work: Original publication for the exact primary dataset and the direct baseline literature our work extends.

authors: Z. Han; C. Zhang; L. Gao; Z. Zeng; M. K. Ng; B. Zhang; J. Chanussot
title: Multi-Source Collaborative Domain Generalization for Cross-Scene Remote Sensing Image Classification
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
method: Multi-source collaborative DG with adversarial augmentation and model diversification
main_finding: Reports improved cross-scene generalization through multi-source augmentation and diversification.
limitation: Uses a specialized multisource DG architecture and different data assumptions from our simpler interventions.
relevance_to_our_work: Direct recent remote-sensing DG comparison.

authors: Yang Li; Zhang Li; Ang Su; Kun Wang; Zi Wang; Qifeng Yu
title: Semisupervised Cross-Domain Remote Sensing Scene Classification via Category-Level Feature Alignment Network
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
main_finding: Uses category-level alignment to reduce cross-domain feature discrepancies.
limitation: Uses labeled/unlabeled target-domain information, unlike our target-unseen source-disjoint DG setting.
relevance_to_our_work: Recent comparison showing another strategy for cross-domain scene robustness.

authors: Yuchi Ma; Shuo Chen; Stefano Ermon; David B. Lobell
title: Transfer Learning in Environmental Remote Sensing
venue: Remote Sensing of Environment
method: Review of transfer-learning approaches and domain shifts
main_finding: Systematizes domain-shift types and transfer-learning strategies in environmental remote sensing.
limitation: Review rather than a controlled benchmark of our specific climate-scene task.
relevance_to_our_work: Primary theoretical support for using pretrained backbones and discussing environmental domain shift.

authors: Deng Xinjie; Burhan Khan; Fazal Ghaffar; Yit Hong Choo; Tao Zhou
title: A Lightweight Deep Learning Model for Aerial Image Classification and Its Application to UAV-based Disaster Management
venue: Procedia Computer Science
main_finding: Demonstrates a lightweight feature-extraction design for UAV disaster-management classification.
limitation: Does not center source-domain generalization or external cross-source validation.
relevance_to_our_work: Recent disaster-classification comparison and deployment-oriented UAV context.

authors: Teng Yang; Song Xiao; Jiahui Qu; Wenqian Dong; Qian Du; Yunsong Li
title: Graph Embedding Interclass Relation-Aware Adaptive Network for Cross-Scene Classification of Multisource Remote Sensing Data
venue: IEEE Transactions on Image Processing
method: Graph embedding and interclass relation-aware adaptation
main_finding: Models class relationships and domain discrepancies for multisource cross-scene classification.
limitation: Unsupervised DA relies on target-domain samples.
relevance_to_our_work: Supports the importance of multisource domain structure and class-aware cross-domain evaluation.

authors: Juepeng Zheng; Yibin Wen; Mengxuan Chen; Shuai Yuan; Weijia Li; Yi Zhao; Wenzhao Wu; Lixian Zhang; Runmin Dong; Haohuan Fu
title: Open-set Domain Adaptation for Scene Classification Using Multi-adversarial Learning
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
main_finding: Addresses cross-domain remote-sensing classification when target domains include unknown classes.
limitation: Open-set DA assumes access to target-domain data and a different label-space problem from our DG protocol.
relevance_to_our_work: Helps distinguish DG from broader real-world cross-domain adaptation settings.

authors: Peng Zhu; Xiangrong Zhang; Xiao Han; Xina Cheng; Jing Gu; Puhua Chen; Licheng Jiao
title: Cross-Domain Classification Based on Frequency Component Adaptation for Remote Sensing Images
venue: Remote Sensing
dataset: AID; CLRS; MLRSN; RSSCN7; NWPU-RESISC45; NaSC-TG2
main_finding: Shows frequency-aware feature alignment can improve cross-domain remote-sensing scene classification.
limitation: Domain adaptation uses target-domain information; our primary DG setting assumes unseen target domains.
relevance_to_our_work: Useful contrast between domain adaptation and true target-unseen domain generalization.

authors: Kaiyang Zhou; Ziwei Liu; Yu Qiao; Tao Xiang; Chen Change Loy
title: Domain Generalization: A Survey
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
main_finding: Defines DG formally and organizes methods including alignment, meta-learning, augmentation, and ensembles.
limitation: Broad survey rather than remote-sensing-specific evidence.
relevance_to_our_work: Primary reference for defining DG and distinguishing it from transfer learning and domain adaptation.

authors: Ishaan Gulrajani; David Lopez-Paz
title: In Search of Lost Domain Generalization
venue: International Conference on Learning Representations
method: DomainBed benchmark; ERM and 14 DG algorithms
evaluation_protocol: Controlled multi-algorithm DG comparison with explicit model-selection strategies
main_finding: Shows carefully implemented and tuned ERM is a very strong baseline and that many DG gains shrink under controlled evaluation.
limitation: Benchmarks are not remote-sensing-specific.
relevance_to_our_work: Direct methodological support for our finding that DG-AUG-V2 and RSC do not consistently beat ERM.

authors: Maryam Rahnemoonfar; Tashnim Chowdhury; Argho Sarkar; Debvrat Varshney; Mohammad Yari; Robin R. Murphy
title: FloodNet: A High Resolution Aerial Imagery Dataset for Post Flood Scene Understanding
venue: IEEE Access
method: Benchmark for image classification, semantic segmentation, and visual question answering
evaluation_protocol: Flooded vs non-flooded scene understanding and pixel-level flood semantics
main_finding: Introduces high-resolution post-Hurricane-Harvey UAV imagery and explicitly distinguishes natural water from flooded roads/buildings.
limitation: Established 2021 benchmark; classification taxonomy does not directly include our Desert class.
relevance_to_our_work: Our independent external UAV benchmark and the source of the segmentation masks used for shortcut analysis.

authors: Kaiyang Zhou; Yongxin Yang; Yu Qiao; Tao Xiang
title: Domain Generalization with MixStyle
venue: International Conference on Learning Representations
main_finding: Mixes instance-level feature statistics to synthesize implicit domains and increase source-domain diversity.
limitation: Original benchmarks differ substantially from remote sensing and climate imagery.
relevance_to_our_work: Foundational citation for the MixStyle variants we tested.

authors: Robert Geirhos; Jörn-Henrik Jacobsen; Claudio Michaelis; Richard Zemel; Wieland Brendel; Matthias Bethge; Felix A. Wichmann
title: Shortcut Learning in Deep Neural Networks
venue: Nature Machine Intelligence
main_finding: Frames many benchmark-to-real-world failures as models learning predictive but non-robust shortcut decision rules.
limitation: General conceptual framework rather than remote-sensing specific quantitative evidence.
relevance_to_our_work: Core conceptual framework for interpreting our ordinary-water/non-flooded-road contextual shortcut evidence.

authors: Zeyi Huang; Haohan Wang; Eric P. Xing; Dong Huang
title: Self-Challenging Improves Cross-Domain Generalization
venue: European Conference on Computer Vision
main_finding: Suppresses dominant predictive features during training to encourage alternative features that may generalize better across domains.
limitation: Original evidence comes from standard DG benchmarks, not heterogeneous remote-sensing sources.
relevance_to_our_work: Foundational citation for our RSC implementation and multi-seed evaluation.

authors: Christos Kyrkou; Theocharis Theocharides
title: EmergencyNet: Efficient Aerial Image Classification for Drone-Based Emergency Monitoring Using Atrous Convolutional Feature Fusion
venue: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
method: Lightweight CNN with atrous convolutional feature fusion
evaluation_protocol: Emergency/disaster aerial image classification with deployment-efficiency analysis
main_finding: Shows efficient UAV disaster classification can retain strong accuracy while substantially reducing computational requirements.
limitation: Focuses on efficient within-benchmark classification rather than source-disjoint robustness.
relevance_to_our_work: Important UAV disaster-classification baseline and application motivation.

authors: Mark Sandler; Andrew Howard; Menglong Zhu; Andrey Zhmoginov; Liang-Chieh Chen
title: MobileNetV2: Inverted Residuals and Linear Bottlenecks
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
evaluation_protocol: Image classification and downstream transfer benchmarks
main_finding: Introduces inverted residual blocks and linear bottlenecks for efficient deep feature extraction.
limitation: Architecture paper does not address remote-sensing domain shift directly.
relevance_to_our_work: Foundational citation for the pretrained backbone used throughout our primary transfer-learning experiments.

authors: Ramprasaath R. Selvaraju; Michael Cogswell; Abhishek Das; Ramakrishna Vedantam; Devi Parikh; Dhruv Batra
title: Grad-CAM: Visual Explanations from Deep Networks via Gradient-Based Localization
venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
main_finding: Uses target-class gradients flowing into convolutional features to produce spatial explanations for CNN predictions.
limitation: Saliency/localization does not establish causal dependence.
relevance_to_our_work: Foundational method for our 27 frozen Grad-CAM heatmaps.

authors: Derrick Bonafilia; Beth Tellman; Tyler Anderson; Erica Issenberg
title: Sen1Floods11: A Georeferenced Dataset to Train and Test Deep Learning Flood Algorithms for Sentinel-1
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops
main_finding: Introduces a geographically diverse Sentinel-1 flood benchmark spanning multiple biomes, ecoregions, continents, and flood events.
limitation: SAR pixel-level flood mapping differs from our RGB three-class scene classification task.
relevance_to_our_work: Important global flood benchmark demonstrating the need for geographically diverse external flood evaluation.

authors: Maryam Rahnemoonfar; Tashnim Chowdhury; Robin Murphy
title: RescueNet: A High Resolution UAV Semantic Segmentation Dataset for Natural Disaster Damage Assessment
venue: Scientific Data
method: Dataset with scene classification and dense semantic annotations
main_finding: Provides detailed UAV annotations for buildings, roads, pools, trees, and other post-disaster scene elements.
limitation: Collected primarily after Hurricane Michael and focuses damage assessment rather than source-domain shift.
relevance_to_our_work: Recent UAV disaster benchmark useful for discussing external scene understanding and annotation richness.

authors: Ritwik Gupta; Bryce Goodman; Nirav Patel; Ricky Hosfelt; Sandra Sajeev; Eric Heim; Jigar Doshi; Keane Lucas; Howie Choset; Matthew Gaston
title: Creating xBD: A Dataset for Assessing Building Damage from Satellite Imagery
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops
method: Large-scale building localization and damage classification benchmark
main_finding: Introduces a large disaster dataset spanning multiple disaster types, countries, and environmental conditions.
limitation: Building-damage/change-detection objective differs from our scene-level climate taxonomy.
relevance_to_our_work: Supports the value of broad event/source diversity for robust disaster-imagery models.

authors: Gui-Song Xia; Jingwen Hu; Fan Hu; Baoguang Shi; Xiang Bai; Yanfei Zhong; Liangpei Zhang; Xiaoqiang Lu
title: AID: A Benchmark Data Set for Performance Evaluation of Aerial Scene Classification
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
method: Large aerial-scene benchmark with classical and deep-learning baselines
main_finding: Provides a large and diverse aerial benchmark designed to overcome saturation of earlier small scene datasets.
limitation: Conventional random benchmark evaluation does not directly measure unseen-source robustness.
relevance_to_our_work: Canonical aerial scene-classification dataset and methodological precedent for our task.

authors: Gong Cheng; Junwei Han; Xiaoqiang Lu
title: Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification: Benchmark and State of the Art
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE
method: Benchmark dataset plus broad scene-classification review
main_finding: Introduces NWPU-RESISC45 with substantial within-class variation and between-class similarity.
limitation: Benchmark partitions primarily assess within-dataset classification rather than explicit source shift.
relevance_to_our_work: Foundational benchmark and taxonomy for remote-sensing scene classification.

authors: Weixun Zhou; Shawn Newsam; Congmin Li; Zhenfeng Shao
title: PatternNet: A Benchmark Dataset for Performance Evaluation of Remote Sensing Image Retrieval
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
method: Large-scale image retrieval benchmark and deep-feature evaluation
main_finding: Addresses scale and saturation limitations of earlier remote-sensing benchmark collections.
limitation: Designed primarily for retrieval rather than climate-scene classification.
relevance_to_our_work: Useful evidence that dataset scale/diversity strongly influence learned remote-sensing representations.

authors: Patrick Helber; Benjamin Bischke; Andreas Dengel; Damian Borth
title: EuroSAT: A Novel Dataset and Deep Learning Benchmark for Land Use and Land Cover Classification
venue: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
main_finding: Provides a publicly available Sentinel-2 benchmark and demonstrates high CNN classification performance.
limitation: High within-dataset accuracy does not directly establish cross-source robustness.
relevance_to_our_work: Illustrates the strong benchmark performance that can be achieved on homogeneous satellite datasets.

authors: Gencer Sumbul; Marcela Charfuelan; Begum Demir; Volker Markl
title: BigEarthNet: A Large-Scale Benchmark Archive for Remote Sensing Image Understanding
venue: IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium
main_finding: Introduces one of the first very large Sentinel-2 archives for deep remote-sensing representation learning.
limitation: Multi-label LULC differs from our RGB three-class climate-scene task.
relevance_to_our_work: Important large-scale satellite benchmark and pretraining/data-diversity reference.

authors: Yang Long; Gui-Song Xia; Shengyang Li; Wen Yang; Michael Ying Yang; Xiao Xiang Zhu; Liangpei Zhang; Deren Li
title: On Creating Benchmark Dataset for Aerial Image Interpretation: Reviews, Guidances, and Million-AID
venue: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
main_finding: Demonstrates the importance of scale, taxonomy design, annotation quality, and diversity in aerial benchmarks.
limitation: Scale alone does not guarantee domain robustness.
relevance_to_our_work: Strong dataset-design reference and supports our provenance/dataset-composition emphasis.

authors: Haifeng Li; Xin Dou; Chao Tao; Zhixiang Wu; Jie Chen; Jian Peng; Min Deng; Ling Zhao
title: RSI-CB: A Large-Scale Remote Sensing Image Classification Benchmark Using Crowdsourced Data
venue: Sensors
method: Large-scale crowdsourced benchmark; classical and DCNN baselines
main_finding: Shows that geographically broad crowdsourced benchmarks can improve diversity and support transfer studies.
limitation: Some labeling depends on POI/crowdsourced supervision and manual filtering.
relevance_to_our_work: Supports our emphasis on geographic/source diversity and benchmark composition.

authors: Keiller Nogueira; Otavio A. B. Penatti; Jefersson A. dos Santos
title: Towards Better Exploiting Convolutional Neural Networks for Remote Sensing Scene Classification
venue: Pattern Recognition
method: CNN training, fine-tuning, and fixed feature extraction
main_finding: Finds fine-tuning pretrained CNNs generally provides strong remote-sensing scene representations.
limitation: Predates modern DG protocols and large-scale contemporary remote-sensing benchmarks.
relevance_to_our_work: Foundational evidence motivating transfer learning rather than training every architecture from scratch.

authors: Fan Hu; Gui-Song Xia; Jingwen Hu; Liangpei Zhang
title: Transferring Deep Convolutional Neural Networks for the Scene Classification of High-Resolution Remote Sensing Imagery
venue: Remote Sensing
method: Transfer of pretrained deep CNN representations
main_finding: Shows pretrained CNN representations can transfer effectively to high-resolution remote-sensing scenes.
limitation: Does not test modern source-disjoint external-domain evaluation.
relevance_to_our_work: Early foundational remote-sensing transfer-learning paper.

authors: Ivica Dimitrovski; Ivan Kitanovski; Nikola Simidjievski; Dragi Kocev
title: In-Domain Self-Supervised Learning Improves Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Letters
method: iBOT self-supervised in-domain pretraining with ViTs
evaluation_protocol: Comparison of ImageNet vs in-domain SSL pretraining
main_finding: Shows in-domain remote-sensing pretraining consistently improves downstream performance compared with generic pretraining strategies.
limitation: Focuses representation transfer rather than source-disjoint DG.
relevance_to_our_work: Provides modern context for why source-domain-aware pretraining may outperform generic ImageNet transfer.

authors: Ilke Demir; Krzysztof Koperski; David Lindenbaum; Guan Pang; Jing Huang; Saikat Basu; Forest Hughes; Devis Tuia; Ramesh Raskar
title: DeepGlobe 2018: A Challenge to Parse the Earth Through Satellite Images
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops
method: Benchmark challenge for classification, detection, and segmentation
main_finding: Establishes large-scale satellite understanding tasks and standardized evaluation protocols.
limitation: Benchmark tasks differ from our specific climate three-class problem.
relevance_to_our_work: Important precedent for benchmark-driven satellite image evaluation.

authors: Yansheng Li; Yuning Wu; Gong Cheng; Chao Tao; Bo Dang; Yu Wang; Jiahao Zhang; Chuge Zhang; Yiting Liu; Xu Tang; Jiayi Ma; Yongjun Zhang
title: MEET: A Million-Scale Dataset for Fine-Grained Geospatial Scene Classification With Zoom-Free Remote Sensing Imagery
venue: IEEE/CAA Journal of Automatica Sinica
main_finding: Demonstrates the importance of surrounding spatial context for fixed-resolution geospatial recognition.
limitation: Focuses fine-grained contextual recognition rather than cross-source robustness.
relevance_to_our_work: Recent large-scale evidence that scene context can strongly influence remote-sensing classification.

authors: Georgios Simantiris; Konstantinos Bacharidis; Apostolos Papanikolaou; Petros Giannakakis; Costas Panagiotakis
title: AIFloodSense: A Global Aerial Imagery Dataset for Semantic Segmentation and Understanding of Flooded Environments
venue: Remote Sensing
dataset: AIFloodSense; 470 aerial images; 230 flood events; 64 countries
evaluation_protocol: Diversity-aware flood benchmarking and external testing
main_finding: Shows geographically/event-diverse flood data can generalize better externally than larger but less diverse datasets.
limitation: Compact dataset and different annotation/tasks from our three-class benchmark.
relevance_to_our_work: Extremely relevant recent evidence supporting our argument that diversity and domain composition matter more than headline within-dataset accuracy.

authors: Tamer Saleh; Xingxing Weng; Shimaa Holail; Chen Hao; Gui-Song Xia
title: DAM-Net: Flood Detection from SAR Imagery Using Differential Attention Metric-Based Vision Transformers
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
dataset: S1GFloods; 5,360 pre/post image pairs; 46 events; 6 continents
method: Differential-attention vision transformer for bi-temporal flood detection
main_finding: Introduces S1GFloods and demonstrates strong flood change-detection results across globally distributed events.
limitation: Bi-temporal SAR segmentation differs from single-image RGB scene classification.
relevance_to_our_work: Recent globally diverse flood benchmark illustrating why cross-event diversity is essential.

authors: Nicla Notarangelo; Charlotte Wirion; Frankwin van Winsen
title: STURM-Flood: A Curated Dataset for Deep Learning-Based Flood Extent Mapping Leveraging Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 Imagery
venue: Big Earth Data
evaluation_protocol: Flood extent mapping with Copernicus EMS references
main_finding: Provides curated multi-sensor flood data aimed at robust and reproducible flood mapping.
limitation: Pixel-level extent mapping rather than scene-level climate classification.
relevance_to_our_work: Recent evidence for multi-source/multi-sensor dataset design and external flood evaluation.

authors: Jia Song; Shaohua Gao; Yunqiang Zhu; Chenyan Ma
title: A Survey of Remote Sensing Image Classification Based on CNNs
venue: Big Earth Data
main_finding: Reviews the transition toward CNN-based representation learning for remote-sensing classification.
limitation: Predates modern transformers, foundation models, and current DG methods.
relevance_to_our_work: Useful historical review for establishing the CNN classification evolution preceding our study.

authors: Qionghao Huang; Can Hu
title: Survey on Remote Sensing Scene Classification: From Traditional Methods to Large Generative AI Models
venue: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences
method: Survey covering handcrafted features, CNNs, ViTs, foundation models, VLMs, and generative AI
main_finding: Identifies cross-domain generalization, interpretability, multimodal learning, and standardized evaluation as important current research directions.
limitation: Broad survey rather than task-specific empirical evidence.
relevance_to_our_work: Current high-level reference positioning our work within the newest remote-sensing scene-classification landscape.

authors: Adrian Höhl; Ivica Obadic; Miguel-Ángel Fernández-Torres; Hiba Najjar; Dario Augusto Borges Oliveira; Zeynep Akata; Andreas Dengel; Xiao Xiang Zhu
title: Opening the Black Box: A Systematic Review on Explainable Artificial Intelligence in Remote Sensing
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Magazine
method: Systematic review of XAI methods, interpretation practices, and evaluation
main_finding: Identifies trends, scientific uses, evaluation methods, and major challenges for XAI in remote sensing.
limitation: Review paper; does not provide task-specific causal evidence for saliency maps.
relevance_to_our_work: Primary remote-sensing-specific reference for explaining why Grad-CAM should be interpreted cautiously.

authors: Xiaowei Gu; Abdulrahman Kerim; Jinghao Zhang; Jungong Han; Qiang Shen; Peter M. Atkinson; Ce Zhang
title: Self-Organising Explainable Multi-View Representation Learning for Remote Sensing Scene Classification
venue: Applied Soft Computing
dataset: Optimal-31; WHU-RS; UCMerced; AID; RSI-CB256; PatternNet
method: Transparent multi-view representation learning with evolving fuzzy neural encoders
main_finding: Combines strong scene classification with transparent multi-view representation learning.
limitation: High benchmark accuracy does not directly establish source-disjoint or external-domain robustness.
relevance_to_our_work: Recent evidence connecting scene classification, generalization, and interpretability.

authors: E. Dritsas; M. Trigka
title: From Faithfulness to Validity: Explainable Artificial Intelligence in Remote Sensing
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Magazine
evaluation_protocol: Review of RS-specific XAI assumptions and failure modes
main_finding: Argues that explanations can appear faithful yet remain scientifically invalid when RS-specific spatial, spectral, temporal, and physical structure is ignored.
limitation: Conceptual/review contribution rather than controlled empirical evaluation.
relevance_to_our_work: Direct support for our cautious claim that Grad-CAM is explanatory evidence, not causal proof.

authors: Christoph Schweden; Peter Jung; Xiao Xiang Zhu
title: Assessing Conformal Prediction for Remote Sensing: Application to Local Climate Zone Classification
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
method: Conformal prediction; uncertainty-aware training; active learning
evaluation_protocol: Prediction-set coverage, uncertainty, and active learning
main_finding: Shows conformal prediction can provide statistically grounded prediction sets and useful uncertainty signals for remote-sensing classification.
limitation: Local Climate Zone classification differs from our climate-disaster taxonomy.
relevance_to_our_work: Supports future uncertainty/calibration analysis and the need to go beyond confidence scores.

authors: Xiaoyan Zhou; Tao Tang; Janne Heikkilä; Li Liu; Yuli Sun; Gangyao Kuang
title: Uncertainty-Aware Dynamic Multi-Prototype Representation for Out-of-Distribution Detection in SAR Imagery
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
main_finding: Explicitly models uncertainty and prototypes to improve recognition of out-of-distribution SAR samples.
limitation: SAR target recognition differs from RGB aerial scene classification.
relevance_to_our_work: Recent remote-sensing evidence that high confidence must be complemented by explicit OOD-awareness.

authors: Tahsin Hossain; Tan Yigitcanlar; Niklas Tilly; Filip Biljecki
title: Trustworthy Transfer Learning in GeoAI: Assessing Pretrained Models for Rooftop Solar PV Mapping Under Geographic Domain Shift
venue: Journal of Geovisualization and Spatial Analysis
dataset: US-pretrained model transferred to Brisbane imagery
method: Transfer learning with independent geographic evaluation
evaluation_protocol: Development + independent test evaluation under geographic domain shift
main_finding: Shows local transfer learning can improve performance while residual false positives, misses, and uncertainty remain important for trustworthy deployment.
limitation: Single rooftop-PV application and limited geographic test scope.
relevance_to_our_work: Very recent direct support for our argument that improved accuracy alone is insufficient evidence of robustness.

authors: Yaniv Ovadia; Emily Fertig; Jie Ren; Zachary Nado; D. Sculley; Sebastian Nowozin; Joshua Dillon; Balaji Lakshminarayanan; Jasper Snoek
title: Can You Trust Your Model's Uncertainty? Evaluating Predictive Uncertainty Under Dataset Shift
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
evaluation_protocol: Accuracy and calibration under increasing dataset shift
main_finding: Shows predictive uncertainty and calibration can degrade substantially under dataset shift; ensembles are among the strongest approaches studied.
limitation: General vision/ML benchmark rather than remote sensing.
relevance_to_our_work: Foundational support for treating high confidence on shifted UAV imagery cautiously.

authors: Chuan Guo; Geoff Pleiss; Yu Sun; Kilian Q. Weinberger
title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
venue: Proceedings of the 34th International Conference on Machine Learning
evaluation_protocol: Expected calibration error and classification accuracy
main_finding: Shows modern deep networks are often overconfident and that temperature scaling is an effective post-hoc calibration baseline.
limitation: In-distribution calibration does not guarantee calibration under domain shift.
relevance_to_our_work: Important theoretical reference for interpreting probability outputs and future calibration work.

authors: Pang Wei Koh; Shiori Sagawa; Henrik Marklund; Sang Michael Xie; Marvin Zhang; Akshay Balsubramani; Weihua Hu; Michihiro Yasunaga; Richard Lanas Phillips; Irena Gao; Tony Lee; Etienne David; Ian Stavness; Wei Guo; Berton Earnshaw; Imran Haque; Sara Beery; Jure Leskovec; Anshul Kundaje; Emma Pierson; Sergey Levine; Chelsea Finn; Percy Liang
title: WILDS: A Benchmark of in-the-Wild Distribution Shifts
venue: Proceedings of the 38th International Conference on Machine Learning
evaluation_protocol: In-distribution vs naturally shifted test domains
main_finding: Shows major ID-to-OOD performance gaps persist across real-world applications even when using robustness methods.
limitation: Broad benchmark; only a subset is geospatial.
relevance_to_our_work: Canonical evidence supporting source-disjoint and external evaluation instead of relying on IID testing.

authors: Oscar Mañas; Alexandre Lacoste; Xavier Giró-i-Nieto; David Vazquez; Pau Rodríguez
title: Seasonal Contrast: Unsupervised Pre-Training from Uncurated Remote Sensing Data
venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision
main_finding: Uses temporal/seasonal invariance to learn effective in-domain remote-sensing representations without labels.
limitation: Representation-learning objective differs from source-disjoint robustness evaluation.
relevance_to_our_work: Supports the argument that ImageNet is not the only useful source of transferable representations for EO.

authors: Kumar Ayush; Burak Uzkent; Chenlin Meng; Kumar Tanmay; Marshall Burke; David Lobell; Stefano Ermon
title: Geography-Aware Self-Supervised Learning
venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision
method: Contrastive learning using temporal alignment and geolocation pretext tasks
main_finding: Shows spatiotemporal and geographic metadata can improve self-supervised remote-sensing representation learning.
limitation: Pretraining study rather than explicit source-domain generalization benchmark.
relevance_to_our_work: Supports geographic/source-aware representation learning.

authors: Yezhen Cong; Samar Khanna; Chenlin Meng; Patrick Liu; Erik Rozi; Yutong He; Marshall Burke; David Lobell; Stefano Ermon
title: SatMAE: Pre-Training Transformers for Temporal and Multi-Spectral Satellite Imagery
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
main_finding: Demonstrates strong gains from adapting masked autoencoding to temporal and multispectral satellite data.
limitation: Does not specifically test our UAV/source-disjoint task.
relevance_to_our_work: Modern evidence for domain-specific EO pretraining.

authors: Anthony Fuller; Koreen Millard; James Green
title: CROMA: Remote Sensing Representations with Contrastive Radar-Optical Masked Autoencoders
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
main_finding: Shows complementary contrastive and reconstruction objectives improve uni- and multimodal EO representations.
limitation: Multimodal sensor setting differs from our RGB UAV scene-classification pipeline.
relevance_to_our_work: Demonstrates how multimodal pretraining can improve general-purpose remote-sensing representations.

authors: Fan Liu; Delong Chen; Zhangqingyun Guan; Xiaocong Zhou; Jiale Zhu; Qiaolin Ye; Liyong Fu; Jun Zhou
title: RemoteCLIP: A Vision Language Foundation Model for Remote Sensing
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
evaluation_protocol: Zero-shot, few-shot, linear probing, retrieval, counting
main_finding: Shows remote-sensing-specific vision-language pretraining substantially improves zero-shot and retrieval performance.
limitation: Foundation-model benchmark differs from our supervised three-class pipeline.
relevance_to_our_work: Important modern reference showing stronger pretrained representations can improve cross-domain generalization.

authors: Xin Guo; Jiangwei Lao; Bo Dang; Yingying Zhang; Lei Yu; Lixiang Ru; Liheng Zhong; Ziyuan Huang; Kang Wu; Dingxiang Hu; Huimei He; Jian Wang; Jingdong Chen; Ming Yang; Yongjun Zhang; Yansheng Li
title: SkySense: A Multi-Modal Remote Sensing Foundation Model Towards Universal Interpretation for Earth Observation Imagery
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
main_finding: Reports broad generalization across sensors, modalities, temporal settings, and downstream tasks.
limitation: Massive pretraining/data scale is far beyond our course-project compute setting.
relevance_to_our_work: Shows the current direction toward representations that explicitly account for domain/modality diversity.

authors: Favyen Bastani; Piper Wolters; Ritwik Gupta; Joe Ferdinando; Aniruddha Kembhavi
title: SatlasPretrain: A Large-Scale Dataset for Remote Sensing Image Understanding
venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision
main_finding: Shows remote-sensing-specific pretraining improves average downstream performance substantially over ImageNet.
limitation: Broad multi-task pretraining rather than a controlled source-disjoint classification study.
relevance_to_our_work: Supports the idea that in-domain EO pretraining could be a stronger future baseline than ImageNet MobileNetV2.

authors: Alexandre Lacoste; Nils Lehmann; Pau Rodriguez; Evan David Sherwin; Hannah Kerner; Björn Lütjens; Jeremy Andrew Irvin; David Dao; Hamed Alemohammad; Alexandre Drouin; Mehmet Gunturkun; Gabriel Huang; David Vazquez; Dava Newman; Yoshua Bengio; Stefano Ermon; Xiao Xiang Zhu
title: GEO-Bench: Toward Foundation Models for Earth Monitoring
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems Datasets and Benchmarks Track
dataset: GEO-Bench; six classification + six segmentation tasks
method: Standardized benchmark for pretrained EO representations
evaluation_protocol: Aggregated evaluation across 12 EO downstream tasks
main_finding: Provides a standardized methodology for evaluating foundation-model representations across diverse EO tasks.
limitation: Downstream benchmark aggregation differs from our source-disjoint climate-scene protocol.
relevance_to_our_work: Supports rigorous, multi-dataset evaluation rather than single-benchmark headline accuracy.

authors: Guillaume Astruc; Nicolas Gonthier; Clément Mallet; Loic Landrieu
title: AnySat: One Earth Observation Model for Many Resolutions, Scales, and Modalities
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
main_finding: Shows one model can generalize across highly heterogeneous resolutions, scales, modalities, and external datasets.
limitation: Much larger pretraining regime and broader task scope than our TensorFlow classification system.
relevance_to_our_work: Highly relevant modern evidence that domain diversity should be built directly into EO representation learning.

authors: Minh Kha Do; Kang Han; Phu Lai; Khoa T. Phan; Wei Xiang
title: RobSense: A Robust Multi-Modal Foundation Model for Remote Sensing with Static, Temporal, and Incomplete Data Adaptability
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
method: Multimodal masked autoencoding + temporal alignment + latent reconstruction
evaluation_protocol: Classification, segmentation, change detection; complete and missing-data settings
main_finding: Maintains strong performance across diverse input types and increasingly incomplete sensor observations.
limitation: Robustness is primarily modality/input-completeness robustness rather than our source-provenance shift.
relevance_to_our_work: Modern example of explicitly designing EO models for robustness rather than only IID accuracy.

authors: Utkarsh Mall; Bharath Hariharan; Kavita Bala
title: Change-Aware Sampling and Contrastive Learning for Satellite Images
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
method: Change-aware contrastive loss + geographically informed data sampling
main_finding: Shows geographic sampling strategy and temporal-change awareness materially affect representation quality.
limitation: Self-supervised representation study rather than explicit DG testing.
relevance_to_our_work: Strong support for our finding that source/geographic dataset composition affects learned representations.

authors: Sara A. Al-Emadi; Yin Yang; Ferda Ofli
title: Benchmarking Object Detectors under Real-World Distribution Shifts in Satellite Imagery
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
platform_domain: Satellite imagery; climate zones, disasters, and geographic regions
method: Benchmarking modern object detectors under real-world spatial distribution shifts
evaluation_protocol: Source-domain training with evaluation on unseen geographic/climate/disaster domains
main_finding: Demonstrates substantial detector degradation under realistic geographic and environmental shifts.
limitation: Object detection differs from our scene-level three-class classification task.
relevance_to_our_work: Direct support for evaluating remote-sensing models under real source/geographic shifts rather than IID splits.

authors: Kang Liu; Jian Yang; Shengyang Li
title: Remote-Sensing Cross-Domain Scene Classification: A Dataset and Benchmark
venue: Remote Sensing
evaluation_protocol: Scene classification across distinct remote-sensing domains/modalities
main_finding: Shows major performance challenges arise when scene classifiers must transfer across imaging domains.
limitation: Its domains and class taxonomy differ from our UAV/satellite climate-scene composition.
relevance_to_our_work: One of the most direct benchmark precedents for our source-aware cross-domain scene evaluation.

authors: Junjue Wang; Zhuo Zheng; Ailong Ma; Xiaoyan Lu; Yanfei Zhong
title: LoveDA: A Remote Sensing Land-Cover Dataset for Domain Adaptive Semantic Segmentation
venue: Proceedings of the Neural Information Processing Systems Track on Datasets and Benchmarks
dataset: LoveDA; 5,987 high-resolution images; urban and rural domains
main_finding: Demonstrates that geographical environment changes and class-distribution differences substantially challenge transferability.
limitation: Segmentation rather than scene classification.
relevance_to_our_work: Strong precedent for defining domains through geographic/environmental differences.

authors: Junshi Xia; Naoto Yokoya; Bruno Adriano; Clifford Broni-Bediako
title: OpenEarthMap: A Benchmark Dataset for Global High-Resolution Land Cover Mapping
venue: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
dataset: OpenEarthMap; 5,000 aerial/satellite images; 97 regions; 44 countries; 6 continents
method: Land-cover segmentation plus unsupervised domain-adaptation benchmarking
main_finding: Provides a geographically diverse benchmark explicitly designed to support worldwide model generalization.
limitation: Land-cover segmentation differs from our scene-classification objective.
relevance_to_our_work: Excellent example of geographic diversity and external-region evaluation.

authors: Nur Nafiiyah; Agus Harjoko; Achmad Nizar Hidayanto
title: Cross-Dataset Generalization of ConvNeXt-Tiny for Remote Sensing Scene Classification
venue: Engineering, Technology & Applied Science Research
method: ImageNet-pretrained ConvNeXt-Tiny compared with ResNet50, DenseNet121, and MobileNetV2
evaluation_protocol: In-dataset and cross-dataset evaluation without target fine-tuning
main_finding: Shows that strong IID scene-classification performance does not automatically translate into equal cross-dataset robustness.
limitation: Evaluation uses shared classes between two conventional scene benchmarks rather than disaster imagery.
relevance_to_our_work: Very direct modern precedent for our argument that cross-dataset evaluation exposes information hidden by random test splits.

authors: Gordon Christie; Neil Fendley; James Wilson; Ryan Mukherjee
title: Functional Map of the World
venue: IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
dataset: fMoW; more than one million images; more than 200 countries; 63 categories
main_finding: Demonstrates the scale and geographic diversity needed for real-world satellite scene understanding.
limitation: Functional land-use labels differ from climate and disaster categories.
relevance_to_our_work: Important global-scale example showing how geography, time, and metadata affect satellite recognition.

authors: Xiao Xiang Zhu; Jingliang Hu; Chunping Qiu; Yilei Shi; Jian Kang; Lichao Mou; Hossein Bagheri; Matthias Haberle; Yuansheng Hua; Rong Huang; Lloyd Hughes; Hao Li; Yao Sun; Guichen Zhang; Shiyao Han; Michael Schmitt; Yuanyuan Wang
title: So2Sat LCZ42: A Benchmark Data Set for the Classification of Global Local Climate Zones
venue: IEEE Geoscience and Remote Sensing Magazine
dataset: So2Sat LCZ42; approximately 500,000 patches; 42 major urban regions plus additional areas
main_finding: Provides globally distributed multisensor data for studying scalable climate-zone classification.
limitation: Urban climate-zone taxonomy differs from our three climate-scene classes.
relevance_to_our_work: Supports geographically distributed training/evaluation and climate-related remote-sensing classification.

authors: Michael Schmitt; Lloyd H. Hughes; Chunping Qiu; Xiao Xiang Zhu
title: SEN12MS – A Curated Dataset of Georeferenced Multi-Spectral Sentinel-1/2 Imagery for Deep Learning and Data Fusion
venue: ISPRS Annals of the Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing and Spatial Information Sciences
platform_domain: Sentinel-1 SAR + Sentinel-2 multispectral + MODIS land cover
evaluation_protocol: Data distributed across inhabited continents and meteorological seasons
main_finding: Addresses limitations in spatial coverage, diversity, and sample count of earlier remote-sensing datasets.
limitation: Dataset contribution rather than a dedicated cross-domain classification experiment.
relevance_to_our_work: Supports our emphasis on dataset composition, source diversity, and seasonal/geographic coverage.

authors: Christopher F. Brown; Steven P. Brumby; Brookie Guzder-Williams; Tanya Birch; Samantha Brooks Hyde; Joseph Mazzariello; Wanda Czerwinski; Valerie J. Pasquarella; Robert Haertel; Simon Ilyushchenko; Kurt Schwehr; Mikaela Weisse; Fred Stolle; Craig Hanson; Oliver Guinan; Rebecca Moore; Alexander M. Tait
title: Dynamic World, Near real-time global 10 m land use land cover mapping
venue: Scientific Data
dataset: Global Sentinel-2 training and validation imagery
evaluation_protocol: Global stratified training and unseen validation data
main_finding: Demonstrates operational deep-learning classification at global scale using geographically and ecologically diverse training/validation data.
limitation: Land-cover taxonomy and global mapping differ from our source-disjoint disaster-scene objective.
relevance_to_our_work: Strong example of deliberately designing data collection for global ecological/geographic diversity.

authors: Gonzalo Mateo-Garcia; Joshua Veitch-Michaelis; Lewis Smith; Silviu Vlad Oprea; Guy Schumann; Yarin Gal; Atılım Güneş Baydin; Dietmar Backes
title: Towards global flood mapping onboard low cost satellites with machine learning
venue: Scientific Reports
method: CNN flood segmentation with onboard low-power inference
evaluation_protocol: Training on global events and testing on independent flood locations
main_finding: Demonstrates flood models on geographically independent events rather than only random image partitions.
limitation: Pixel-level segmentation rather than scene-level classification.
relevance_to_our_work: Excellent precedent for our external FloodNet evaluation philosophy.

authors: B. Tellman; J. A. Sullivan; C. Kuhn; A. J. Kettner; C. S. Doyle; G. R. Brakenridge; T. A. Erickson; D. A. Slayback
title: Satellite imaging reveals increased proportion of population exposed to floods
venue: Nature
evaluation_protocol: Global multi-event flood mapping with independent accuracy assessment
main_finding: Provides globally observed flood extent across hundreds of heterogeneous real disaster events.
limitation: Not a deep-learning scene-classification study.
relevance_to_our_work: Provides strong evidence for the enormous variability of real flood environments and events.

authors: Ronny Hänsch; Jacob Arndt; Dalton Lunga; Matthew Gibb; Tyler Pedelose; Arnold Boedihardjo; Desiree Petrie; Todd M. Bacastow
title: SpaceNet 8 - The Detection of Flooded Roads and Buildings
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops
dataset: SpaceNet 8; flooded buildings and roads; approximately 850 km²
main_finding: Combines flood detection with operationally important building and road understanding.
limitation: Task is structured detection/segmentation rather than our three-class scene classification.
relevance_to_our_work: Supports disaster imagery evaluation using real post-event environmental context.

authors: Demetris Shianios; Christos Kyrkou
title: Advancing efficiency and accuracy in aerial image classification for disaster incidents with SqueezeViT and UAVDisaster36K benchmark
venue: Neurocomputing
evaluation_protocol: Disaster image classification with performance/efficiency benchmarking
main_finding: Provides a substantially larger modern UAV disaster classification benchmark and compares accuracy with deployment efficiency.
limitation: Does not isolate satellite-to-UAV domain transfer.
relevance_to_our_work: Directly relevant recent UAV disaster scene-classification benchmark.

authors: Norah Alsaaran; Adel Soudani
title: Deep Learning Image-Based Classification for Post-Earthquake Damage Level Prediction Using UAVs
venue: Sensors
main_finding: Shows lightweight pretrained CNNs can provide efficient real-time UAV disaster classification.
limitation: Single disaster type and damage taxonomy.
relevance_to_our_work: Useful comparison for lightweight transfer learning in UAV disaster imagery.

authors: Zhaobin Wang; Rui Wang; Yongke Lv; Yaonan Zhang; Ye Zhu
title: DBE-SSDNet: A Dual-Branch Desert Segmentation Model With Structured State-Space Duality for Satellite Remote Sensing
venue: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
dataset: Landsat 8 imagery from multiple desert systems
main_finding: Reports strong performance across distinct desert boundary conditions and geographic regions.
limitation: Segmentation and boundary extraction differ from scene-level Desert classification.
relevance_to_our_work: Recent evidence for explicitly testing desert models across different geographical conditions.

authors: Zhijia Zheng; Xiuyuan Zhang; Jiajun Li; Eslam Ali; Jinsongdi Yu; Shihong Du
title: Global perspectives on sand dune patterns: Scale-adaptable classification using Landsat imagery and deep learning strategies
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
evaluation_protocol: Large-scale classification of globally distributed sand-dune patterns
main_finding: Demonstrates deep-learning classification across geographically diverse global desert environments.
limitation: Dune morphology classes differ from our broad Desert scene label.
relevance_to_our_work: Provides direct literature support for the heterogeneity within the apparently simple Desert category.

authors: Farah Chouikhi; Ali Ben Abbes; Imed Riadh Farah
title: An end-to-end pipeline based on a Two-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network for monitoring desertification in Africa using remote sensing images
venue: Environmental Modelling & Software
main_finding: Demonstrates CNN-based desertification monitoring over large spatial and temporal extents.
limitation: MODIS resolution and desertification labels differ from our RGB scene-level dataset.
relevance_to_our_work: Supports the Desert component of our climate-scene classification literature.

authors: Fouzi Harrou; Benamar Bouyeddou; Nabil Zerrouki; Abdelkader Dairi; Ying Sun; Yacine Zerrouki
title: Detecting the signs of desertification with Landsat imagery: A semi-supervised anomaly detection approach
venue: Results in Engineering
dataset: Multitemporal Landsat imagery from Biskra, Algeria
method: Semi-supervised anomaly detection with OCSVM and alternative detectors
evaluation_protocol: Desertification detection plus bootstrap confidence intervals
main_finding: Shows desertification can be detected from multispectral temporal signals without requiring large labeled desertification datasets.
limitation: Regional anomaly-detection task rather than cross-domain scene classification.
relevance_to_our_work: Broadens our Desert literature beyond conventional supervised CNN classification.

authors: Abdolhossein Boali; Hamid Reza Asgari; Ali Mohammadian Behbahani; Abdolrassoul Salmanmahiny; Babak Naimi
title: Remotely sensed desertification modeling using ensemble of machine learning algorithms
venue: Remote Sensing Applications: Society and Environment
evaluation_protocol: Comparison and ensemble of multiple desertification models
main_finding: Uses model ensembles to reduce uncertainty in remote-sensing desertification assessment.
limitation: Environmental modeling rather than RGB scene recognition.
relevance_to_our_work: Useful contrast with single-model classification and supports discussion of uncertainty.

authors: Hao Zhan; Yingqi Xue; Xiaoqiang Yuan; Jinsongdi Yu; Zhijia Zheng
title: Cross-temporal classification of sand dune/sheet in the Belt and Road Initiative drylands based on deep learning domain adaptation
venue: International Journal of Digital Earth
dataset: Dryland imagery across 22 Belt and Road Initiative countries and multiple years
method: Fourier-based spectral adaptation plus TransUNet self-training
evaluation_protocol: Cross-temporal classification under spectral domain shift
main_finding: Directly demonstrates that spectral/domain shifts across time impair desert mapping and motivates domain-adaptation strategies.
limitation: Temporal domain adaptation differs from our source/provenance-domain shift.
relevance_to_our_work: Highly relevant evidence that even within dryland/desert imagery, distribution shift materially changes classification behavior.
